newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's hard-left warn Prodi after Berlusconi move.
newsitem.headline: Italy's hard-left warn Prodi after Berlusconi move.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi praised opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi on Sunday for saying he was willing to back a government mini-budget providing the measures helped Italy in Europe.

However Fausto Bertinotti, the leader of the hard left Communist Refoundation party which holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament, warned Prodi against what it called Berlusconi's "poisoned chalice."

And the far-right National Alliance party, members of Berlusconi's Freedom Alliance, added that the government should think more about changing "direction and men" rather than seeking help from the opposition.

Prodi said in a statement that "the willingness shown by the leader of the Freedom Alliance, Silvio Berlusconi, to vote for the government's public finance provisions is an act of responsibility that does him honour."

"I am certain that, if confirmed, such a willingness will allow the country to achieve without pointless and dangerous conflicts the objectives needed to enter the single currency with the strongest European economies."

Berlusconi told reporters on Saturday that his opposition might be prepared to help Prodi with a mini-budget needed to bring Italy's deficit down to levels that would enable the country to meet single currency requirements.
He repeated on Sunday that the opposition was concerned about the country's interests above all.
He said it was "willing to lend a hand to the government to pass a budget needed to get out of this grave situation and lead the country into the single currency."
But Berlusconi said the government would have to address pressing structural problems of public spending.
Communist Refoundation is opposed to the mini-budget and any cuts in public spending or tax hikes.
It has also called for a negotiated delay to the start of EMU and threatened to withdraw its support if the government cuts a deal with the opposition.
"Prodi is making a very serious error in accepting the poisoned chalice offered by Berlusconi," said Bertinotti.
"Lets make a definite forecast right from the start: A budget voted for by the right will not get the backing of Refoundation, and viceversa."

"We are simple and straightforward people. We know that what goes down well on the right cannot be good for the left. What is good for the bosses is not good for the unemployed and the workers," Bertinotti added.
Berlusconi's centre-right allies pointed out that the opposition was not offering carte-blanche co-operation.
"Berlusconi did not say he would approve whatever the government proposes but that Europe is to the advantage of all Italians," said CCD senator Francesco d'Onofrio.

Prodi said on Friday that his government would have a figure for the mini-budget within the next few weeks. "I have said that, for now, we are looking at a figure that ranges between six trillion and 14.5 trillion lire," he said.
The Bank of Italy said on Friday that 15 trillion lire must be sliced from the budget deficit if Italy was to cut its deficit to GDP ratio to the three percent required.

A decision on which countries will qualify for EMU founder membership will be made in early 1998 on the basis of their 1997 accounts. Countries must meet set targets on inflation, exchange rates, interest rates, deficits and public debt.
